_note: Run: python3 bin/mutate.py --spec mutations/extract-features.json (the driver's control logic is standard-library only, so no torch venv is needed -- the referenced tests are the pure-logic ones in tests.test_extract_features). This is bin/extract-features.py, the one-run driver that walks every method shipping a feature_provider.py and saves its val features under <out>/<method>/. These mutations prove its guards are not vacuous: discovery matches the provider as a whole filename (a decoy must not count); a method with no checkpoint is skipped with a reason rather than silently dropped; the exit status is nonzero unless every discovered method actually produced features (a skip or an error must never read as success in a paper run); each method runs in its own venv (isolation), a worker's ok result is trusted only when it says ok, and a crashed worker's stderr is carried into the error rather than dropped. The real subprocess path on a real method (which imports the shared adapterlib) is covered by tests.test_method_14_simclrv1.TestFeatureProvider.test_the_isolated_driver_run_extracts_this_method_end_to_end.

targets.label: discovery matches the provider filename as a substring, so a decoy (test_feature_provider.py / feature_provider.py.bak) counts as a provider
a method with no checkpoint is marked ready instead of skipped, so a missing method is dropped silently
a skip no longer fails the run, so a silently missing method reads as success
an error no longer fails the run, so a provider that ran and crashed reads as success
a method's own venv is ignored, so every method runs in the driver's interpreter (defeating isolation)
a worker's ok result is not trusted, so a successful extraction is misreported
a crashed worker's stderr is dropped from the error, hiding why it failed
